correctness.rationale: For all n>=3, polynomial Euler identity mod2 gives E_n(t)=(1+t)^(n-1) mod2; Lucas gives iff n-1 power of two, A(n,1) gives exactly one factor 2 except n=3. For odd common p, n! == 2 mod p forces p>n>=5. Rational cumulants with invertible denominators give n+1 == 3(n-1)^2 == 15(n-1)^4 mod p, hence (3n-1)(n-2)==0, 5(n-1)^2==1, p=11, n==4 mod11, contradiction. Direct rows n3 and n4 finish. Standalone exact checker passed 1462 assertions through n=240, with inclusion-exclusion and moments crosschecks. Infinite proof is algebraic.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Progression-sum congruences allow coefficient cancellations and do not imply congruences for every coefficient. Local polynomial congruences modulo powers of t-1 are different from reduction of all intermediate coefficients modulo each integer prime. Neither comparison yields a stronger theorem implying the proposed classification. The prime-row congruence excludes p as a common divisor for n=p but says nothing about arbitrary row n or other primes, hence does not determine the complete gcd.

value.rationale: Full interior Eulerian-row gcd is a canonical integer divisibility invariant, not an arbitrary restriction. The exact all-n classification separates an isolated odd-prime 11 phenomenon from a dyadic family and otherwise unit gcd. The fourth-cumulant obstruction gives a structural explanation for the absence of every other odd prime, above the documented finite table. This supplies natural complete classification and reproducible exact verification.
